title: ASENA analysis program flags a car at Yüksekova carrying 52.5 kg of explosives bound for Istanbul
summary: The Turkish police's ASENA analysis program flagged a car at Yüksekova on 20 March 2022. Officers found 52.5 kg of explosives. The interior minister said that they were bound for Istanbul.
headline: ASENA flags a car at Yüksekova carrying 52.5 kg of explosives
metric: 133 packets, 52.5 kg, of factory-made explosive
brief: On 20 March 2022 officers of the Hakkari Provincial Police Directorate stopped a car at a checkpoint in Yüksekova, Turkey. Work on the directorate's ASENA analysis program had flagged the car. A hidden compartment under the spare-wheel well held 133 packets of factory-made explosive, 52.5 kg in all. The explosive was assessed as PETN-RDX.[1] The driver was a police officer posted in Istanbul. On 20 November 2023 the Hakkari 2nd Heavy Penal Court sentenced him to 21 years in prison for supplying weapons to a terrorist organization. It sentenced four co-defendants to 17.5 years each for the same offense.[2] ASENA was designed to flag drug crime. This find lay outside its purpose. Interior Minister Süleyman Soylu said on 21 March 2022 that police had identified a suspicious vehicle thought to be carrying drugs. He said that the police had used analysis programs, “what they call artificial intelligence”.[3] The head of the police Narcotics Crimes Department spoke in June 2022. He listed the explosives among the finds of operations that, by his account, had started with ASENA.[4] No source records the data that ASENA matched for this car. None of the sources says whether an analyst checked the flag before the stop. The driver spoke in court of “those who informed”, but no informant is reported.[5]
